remaining: ASA Banka fleet/OEM, BBI Smart ATM OEM and count, BAMCARD/BH Mreza current state, ABRS RS sector data, UniCredit BiH, Union banka, tenders

signals.entity: Central Bank of BiH (CBBiH) / IPS BiH
signals.signal: CBBiH went live with the domestic instant payment system (IPS BiH, a TIPS clone) on 20/07/2026. Available from day one to all commercial banks; initial participants Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, Raiffeisen Bank BiH and Sparkasse Bank BiH, together a quarter of banking-sector assets. CBBiH per-transaction fee is lower than the existing giro-clearing fee. Built on the ECB-approved TIPS clone adapted by Banca d'Italia for the Western Balkans, funded via the European Commission/EU Delegation.
signals.implies: Every remaining BiH bank must now do an ISO 20022 / 24x7x365 payments-rail integration, real-time fraud/AML screening and always-on liquidity monitoring. Direct pull for Printec transaction monitoring, AML/compliance and HSM/security, plus POS/acquiring tie-ins as instant + QR arrives at the till.
signals.followup: Get the IPS BiH scheme rulebook (Odluka o pravilima rada instant placanja) for transaction cap, mandatory-join deadline and fraud-control obligations; map which of the remaining ~18 banks have no real-time monitoring.

signals.signal: Nova banka joined IPS BiH on 28/07/2026, becoming the fourth participant eight days after go-live and the first Republika Srpska bank in the scheme. CEO Sinisa Adzic framed it as continued investment in digital solutions.
signals.implies: Onboarding is running bank-by-bank at pace; the ~18 non-connected banks are a rolling pipeline for instant-payments enablement, transaction monitoring and fraud tooling.
signals.followup: Track subsequent CBBiH joiner releases weekly (press/AllNews); identify the integration vendor Nova banka used.

signals.entity: BiH SEPA accession / both entity parliaments
signals.signal: On 28/07/2026 the FBiH Parliament House of Representatives adopted the harmonised set of financial laws after the RS National Assembly had already done so, completing all regulatory preconditions for BiH's formal SEPA application. CBBiH filed the draft application 12/12/2025 and chairs the SEPA Coordination Committee. Governor Selimovic targets SEPA membership by end-2026, with more banks joining IPS BiH through 2027.
signals.source_name: CBBiH press release (bs); CBBiH/Central Banking governor interview
signals.implies: SEPA entry forces IBAN/ISO 20022 migration, SCT/SDD scheme compliance and sanctions/AML screening upgrades across all 22 BiH banks in a compressed window - a country-wide compliance and payments-modernisation programme.
signals.followup: Obtain the texts of the entity payment-services laws (Sluzbeni glasnik) and the CBBiH SEPA roadmap milestones; identify which banks lack ISO 20022 capability.

signals.entity: BiH ATM market (all 22 banks) - CBBiH card-business report
signals.signal: Installed ATMs rose to 1,868 at 31/12/2025 from 1,767 in 2024. The mix shifted sharply: cash-in/cash-out (deposit-capable) ATMs jumped to 567 from 345 (+222, +64% y/y), withdrawal-only fell to 1,281 from 1,294, and bill-payment kiosks collapsed to 20 from 128. POS terminals reached 37,895 (37,647 in merchants, 248 at bank counters) from 35,035. Active cards 2,657,020; 215.1m transactions worth KM 21.1bn; cash at ATM/POS fell to 65% of card turnover from 68%.
signals.source_name: CBBiH, 'Kartičarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini' (Payment Systems Dept.)
signals.implies: Hard primary evidence of a growing, recycler-led ATM market: +222 deposit-capable units in a single year is the single clearest Printec recycler/cash-automation signal in BiH. The bill-payment kiosk collapse (128 to 20) shows those functions being folded into multifunction ATMs.
signals.likelihood: Very high - already happened, trend continuing
signals.followup: Get the 2026 interim data and the per-bank split; identify which banks added the 222 recyclers in 2025 and which OEM supplied them.

signals.entity: CBBiH IPS BiH scheme rulebook (Odluka o pravilima rada)
signals.signal: CBBiH Governing Board decision of 10/07/2026 (7th session) sets the IPS BiH rules: orders must be in BAM; maximum single transaction 5,000.00 BAM; end-to-end settlement within a maximum of 10 seconds, irrevocable and final; the MANDATORY initiation channel is a mobile or electronic payment platform; a QR code may be used to initiate a payment per a specification CBBiH will publish. Participation is compulsory: any bank that executed at least 1 million cumulative transactions across the RTGS (BPRV) and giro-clearing systems between 01/01/2026 and 30/06/2026 must be an IPS BiH participant from 01/01/2027; any bank exceeding 500,000 cumulative transactions in a calendar year must join from 1 July of the following year. Direct participants must have an ESMIG connection, a payment-services licence, a reserve account at CBBiH and pass certification testing.
signals.source_name: CBBiH, 'Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant plaćanja CBBiH' (PDF)
signals.implies: A dated compliance cliff: the largest BiH banks are legally obliged to be live on IPS BiH by 01/01/2027, and every joiner needs a mobile/e-payment front end, an ESMIG link, a QR acceptance scheme and 10-second real-time processing with fraud controls. Directly addressable by Printec digital onboarding/eKYC, transaction monitoring, AML and HSM/security, and by POS/acquiring for QR merchant acceptance.
signals.followup: Identify from CBBiH RTGS/giro statistics which banks cross the 1m-transaction test for H1-2026 (they must be live by 01/01/2027) and which lack a mobile payment platform today; watch for the CBBiH QR-code specification publication.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank International / Addiko Bank AG (incl. Addiko FBiH and Addiko RS)
signals.signal: RBI won the contested takeover of Addiko Bank AG. After the acceptance period expired on 29/07/2026 at 17:00 CEST, RBI had acceptances for 10,831,435 Addiko shares = 56.16% of shares subject to the offer, clearing its reduced minimum threshold of >55%; Alta Group's 1,878,167 shares (9.63% of issued capital) were tendered in. RBI's offer dates from 14/05/2026 under sec. 25a Austrian Takeover Act. NLB's higher competing offer failed to reach its threshold. The formal official result and regulatory approvals are still to follow.
signals.source_name: RBI ad-hoc announcement via EQS News
signals.implies: BiH gets a large in-market bank merger: Raiffeisen Bank dd BiH (already on Temenos core) plus Addiko Bank dd Sarajevo and Addiko Bank ad Banja Luka. Integration means core/channel migration, branch and ATM fleet rationalisation and re-siting, card portfolio and acquiring consolidation, and a single AML/monitoring stack - classic Printec managed-services, ATM refresh and migration territory, and equally a risk that RBI standardises on incumbent group vendors.
signals.followup: Confirm the official result publication and the Austrian/BiH (FBA, ABRS, Competition Council) approval timetable; get Addiko FBiH and Addiko RS branch/ATM counts to size the fleet rationalisation.

signals.entity: Payten (Asseco SEE Group) - BiH ATM services incumbent
signals.signal: Payten publicly positions itself as the BiH ATM market leader for installation and maintenance, stating it maintains circa 1,200 ATMs in Bosnia and Herzegovina and is 'the only service provider on the Bosnian market that maintains all global ATM brands', including Diebold Nixdorf and NCR. The same announcement records a Diebold Nixdorf Cineo ATM delivery to Sparkasse Bank BiH and MF Bank.
signals.implies: Payten/ASEE is the entrenched competitor holding roughly two thirds of BiH's ~1,868 installed ATMs on a managed-service basis, and is the DN channel. Any Printec entry has to be either a displacement play at renewal or a beachhead on the new deposit/recycler wave. Also flags Sparkasse BiH and MF Bank as Diebold Nixdorf estates.
signals.followup: Verify Payten's CURRENT BiH ATM-under-service count from ASEE Group quarterly reports (ASEE reports Payten segment revenue) and identify which banks' service contracts come up for renewal; this 2020 figure needs refreshing.

signals.signal: At its plenary of 19/06/2026 the FATF placed Bosnia and Herzegovina on the list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring (the 'grey list'), citing the need to improve anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing. The FBA states the banking system itself was assessed by MoneyVal as one of the best-regulated parts of BiH and that the reasons relate to the wider legal and institutional framework, but concedes the classification 'may have limited effects on the efficiency of banking services in international business'. An Action Plan of measures applies.
signals.source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo FBiH (FBA) - Moneyval/grey-list notice
signals.implies: Grey-listing forces every BiH bank and its correspondent banks into enhanced due diligence, stronger sanctions/PEP screening, better STR quality and demonstrable transaction monitoring - the strongest AML/compliance demand trigger in the region right now, and it lands at the same moment as instant payments (faster money, less time to screen). Squarely Printec AML/compliance, transaction monitoring and eKYC territory.
signals.likelihood: Certain - already listed; exit takes years
signals.followup: Get the FATF public statement and BiH Action Plan items with their deadlines; check which BiH banks lost or repriced correspondent relationships; approach FBA-supervised banks on monitoring-tool upgrades.

signals.entity: Agencija za bankarstvo FBiH (FBA) - 2026 supervisory expectations
signals.signal: FBA published 'Supervizorska ocekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka u 2026. godini' (Feb-2026, notice 20/02/2026) with 11 priorities. Item 5 requires banks to strengthen digital resilience with regular penetration testing and red-team exercises, multi-layer security controls, data encryption, network segmentation, continuous monitoring, automated attack response, and continuity plans covering rebuilding systems 'from zero', plus explicit third-party/outsourcing risk registers. Item 9 states formal AML compliance is no longer enough and requires transaction-monitoring systems tuned to real BiH client behaviour (cash flows, diaspora remittances, cross-border payments) with improved analytics and automation. Item 10 requires banks to set payment-services development goals in their business strategies and prepare for BiH's SEPA accession.
signals.implies: A named regulator shopping list that matches the Printec catalogue almost line by line: transaction monitoring and AML analytics, HSM/security and encryption, penetration testing, and managed services (with the third-party-risk caveat that outsourcing must be fully documented). Use it as the door-opener with every FBiH bank's CRO/CISO.
signals.followup: Get the ABRS (Republika Srpska) equivalent supervisory expectations for 2026 to cover the other entity; ask FBiH banks which of the 11 items they are behind on.

signals.entity: FBiH banking sector - ATM/POS/branch network (FBA data)
signals.signal: At 31/12/2025 banks operating in FBiH had 1,447 ATMs (1,369 a year earlier, +78) and 28,632 POS terminals (27,412), across 413 branches/higher organisational units (410) and 124 other units (125). RS-headquartered banks' units inside FBiH grew from 19 to 23 branches and from 43 to 62 ATMs, i.e. RS banks added 19 ATMs in the Federation in one year. Individuals' mobile-banking transactions rose to 6,650,858 from 5,581,193 (+19%) worth KM 2.25bn, while ATM cash withdrawals by individuals still rose to 23,595,549 transactions worth KM 6.66bn. Banks filed 528 suspicious transaction reports in 2025 (523 in 2024), but late filings (after the 3-day deadline) fell from 293 to 61.
signals.source_name: FBA, 'Informacija o subjektima bankarskog sistema FBiH na dan 31.12.2025' - Tabele 2, 67, 69, 71
signals.implies: Branch count is flat while ATMs and POS keep growing and mobile use accelerates - the classic 'cash out of the branch, into self-service' pattern Printec sells recyclers and managed services into. RS banks expanding ATMs into FBiH is a cross-entity land-grab worth chasing (Nova banka, Atos, Addiko RS, NLB RS, MF banka).
signals.likelihood: High - trend confirmed two years running
signals.followup: Pull the equivalent ABRS table for Republika Srpska to complete the national fleet picture, and the FBA H1-2026 preliminary data when published.
